overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of scientific theories of consciousness. You'll be asked about the core commitments of global workspace, integrated information, higher-order, and predictive processing theories, and about the adversarial collaboration model.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: According to integrated information theory, what is an experience identical to?

options.html: Information broadcast from a global workspace
options.text: Information broadcast from a global workspace
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Broadcast is the global workspace theory's mechanism.

options.html: A higher-order thought about a mental state
options.text: A higher-order thought about a mental state
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. That's the higher-order theory's account.

options.html: The integrated causal structure of a physical system
options.text: The integrated causal structure of a physical system
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! IIT identifies experience with the cause–effect structure of a maximally integrated substrate.

options.html: The brain's best guess about its sensory input
options.text: The brain's best guess about its sensory input
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. That's the predictive processing account.

forms.stemHtml: On Rosenthal's higher-order thought theory, what makes a mental state conscious?

options.html: Its being broadcast throughout the brain
options.text: Its being broadcast throughout the brain
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. That's the global workspace theory's answer.

options.html: A suitable thought that one is in that state
options.text: A suitable thought that one is in that state
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The higher-order thought needn't itself be conscious.
Sorry, that's incorrect. That's closer to IIT's answer.
Sorry, that's incorrect. The higher-order thought is usually not conscious. Introspection is a special case.

forms.stemHtml: Which of the following are features of an adversarial collaboration? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Rival theorists agree on predictions in advance
options.text: Rival theorists agree on predictions in advance
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The predictions must differ between the theories.
Correct! Preregistration prevents adjusting predictions to fit results.

options.html: Theory-neutral teams collect and analyze the data
options.text: Theory-neutral teams collect and analyze the data
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Separating roles reduces confirmatory bias.

options.html: Each theory's proponents run their own experiments
options.text: Each theory's proponents run their own experiments
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. That's the older model the approach replaces.

options.html: The study's results decide which theory is true
options.text: The study's results decide which theory is true
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Results challenge or support predictions, and interpretations can differ.

forms.stemHtml: What does Seth mean by calling perception a "controlled hallucination"?

options.html: That most of what we perceive isn't really there
options.text: That most of what we perceive isn't really there
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The phrase doesn't mean perception is false.

options.html: That perception depends on drugs or brain damage
options.text: That perception depends on drugs or brain damage
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Seth is describing ordinary perception.

options.html: That perception is prediction held in check by input
options.text: That perception is prediction held in check by input
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Hallucination, on this view, is prediction that has come loose from the input.

options.html: That perception is controlled by conscious choice
options.text: That perception is controlled by conscious choice
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The control comes from sensory signals, not choice.

forms.stemHtml: What is the global neuronal workspace theory's term for the sudden, self-sustaining surge of activity across the workspace network that marks the moment information becomes conscious? Enter one word.

options.feedbackHtml: Correct! On this theory, ignition makes information available for report, memory, and reasoning.

forms.defaultFeedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The theory calls this ignition.

title: Scientific Theories of Consciousness
